notes.body: In Japanese both parents call the baby bōya, literally 'boy', though she was introduced as a girl. At the time it was also used as fond baby-talk for any small child, so the Japanese passes over the mismatch more lightly than 'boy' would in English.
This is a nursing baby's food-cry, banged out with spoon and dish, not real words.
The same storm stood outside the door at the start of the meal, then was drowned out by family noise until the mother heard it again alone.

data.say: Kept three Curious-only notes for what English cannot carry and left the vision undecoded.
